The Discourse on Possession:
Is an Arahant possessed of the four fruits?
Yes, he is.

Is an Arahant endowed with four types of contact, four types of feeling, four types of perception, four types of volition, four types of consciousness, four types of faith, four types of energy, four types of mindfulness, four types of concentration, and four types of wisdom?
One should not say so… [and so on]… Is a Non-returner endowed with three fruits?
“Yes,” you say.
“Does a non-returner possess three types of contact … [and so on] … three types of wisdom?
You must not say so … [and so on].
Is a once-returner endowed with two fruits?
Yes. Is a once-returner endowed with two contacts ... [and so on] ... with two types of wisdom?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is an Arahant endowed with the fruit of stream-entry? Yes.
Is an Arahant a stream-enterer who is "one who returns seven times at most," "one who goes from family to family," or "one with only one seed remaining"?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...Is an Arahant endowed with the fruit of a once-returner?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is an arahant a once-returner?
You should not say so …pe…
Is an arahant endowed with the fruit of non-returning? Yes.

Is an arahant a non-returner—one who attains final nibbāna in the interval, one who attains final nibbāna upon landing, one who attains final nibbāna without exertion, one who attains final nibbāna with exertion, or one who goes upstream to the Akaniṭṭha realm?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is a non-returner endowed with the fruit of stream-entry? Yes.
Is a non-returner (anāgāmī) a stream-enterer (sotāpanna) who is "one who has seven births at most," "one who goes from family to family" (kolaṅkolo), or "one with one seed left" (ekabījī)?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is a non-returner endowed with the fruit of the once-returner (sakadāgāmiphala)?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is a non-returner a once-returner?
You should not say so… [and so on].
Is a once-returner endowed with the fruit of stream-entry? Yes.
Is a once-returner who is a stream-enterer one who has seven births at most, one who goes from family to family, or a one-seeder?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is one who possesses the fruit of stream-entry to be called a “stream-enterer”? Yes.
Is an Arahant endowed with the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes. Is that very same Arahant a stream-enterer?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is one who possesses the fruit of once-returning to be called a “once-returner”? Yes.
Is an Arahant endowed with the fruit of a once-returner?
Yes. Is that very same Arahant a once-returner?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is one who possesses the fruit of non-returning to be called a “non-returner”? Yes.
Is an Arahant endowed with the fruit of non-returning?
Yes. Is that very same Arahant a non-returner?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is one who possesses the fruit of stream-entry to be called a “stream-enterer”? Yes.
Is a non-returner endowed with the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes. Is that very same non-returner a stream-enterer?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is one who possesses the fruit of a once-returner to be called a “once-returner”? Yes.
Is a non-returner endowed with the fruit of once-returning?
Yes. Is that very same non-returner a once-returner? No.
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Is one who is endowed with the fruit of stream-entry to be called a "stream-enterer"? Yes.
Is a once-returner endowed with the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes. Is that very same once-returner a stream-enterer?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is an Arahant possessed of the fruit of stream-entry? Yes.
Is it not the case that the Arahant has transcended the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes, he has.
If the Arahant has indeed transcended the fruit of stream-entry, then certainly you should not say:
“An arahant is endowed with the fruit of stream-entry.
Is an arahant endowed with the fruit of stream-entry because he has transcended it? Yes.

Is an Arahant one who has transcended the path of stream-entry, and has transcended personality-belief, doubt, and adherence to rules and observances, as well as lust, hatred, and delusion leading to states of deprivation, and is thus possessed of them?
One should not say so... [etc. ...
Is an Arahant one who is possessed of the fruit of once-returning?
“Yes.
“But is it not the case that an Arahant has transcended the fruit of a once-returner?
“Yes.”
If an Arahant has transcended the fruit of once-returning, surely it should not be said that "an Arahant is possessed of the fruit of once-returning.
Is an Arahant who has transcended the fruit of once-returning possessed of it?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Does the Arahant transcend the path of the once-returner, and having transcended gross sensual lust and gross ill will, is he possessed of them?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.
Is an Arahant endowed with the fruit of non-returning?
Yes. But is it not the case that an Arahant has transcended the fruit of non-returning?
“Yes.
“If an Arahant has transcended the fruit of non-returning, then surely it should not be said that ‘an Arahant is possessed of the fruit of non-returning.’”
Is an Arahant one who has transcended the fruit of non-returning and yet is possessed of it? Yes.

Is an Arahant one who has transcended the path of non-returning, and having transcended even the residual attachment to sensual desire and the residual attachment to ill will, is he yet possessed of them?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is a non-returner endowed with the fruit of stream-entry? Yes.
Is it not the case that a non-returner has transcended the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes, it is.
If a non-returner has indeed transcended the fruit of stream-entry, then certainly, you should not say: [that he has not].
“One who is a non-returner is endowed with the fruit of stream-entry.
Is a non-returner one who has transcended the fruit of stream-entry and is nevertheless endowed with it? Yes.

Is an Anāgāmī one who has transcended the path of stream-entry, transcended personality-belief (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*), and so forth, up to having transcended the delusion that leads to states of deprivation, yet is still possessed of those [fetters]?
One should not say so... [etc. ...
Is an Anāgāmī possessed of the fruit of a Once-returner (*sakadāgāmiphala*)?
“Yes.
“But is it not the case that a non-returner has transcended the fruit of once-returning?
“Yes.”
If a non-returner has transcended the fruit of once-returning, surely it should not be said that "the non-returner is possessed of the fruit of once-returning.
Is it the case that a non-returner, having transcended the fruit of once-returning, is nevertheless possessed of it?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then has the non-returner transcended the path of the once-returner, and transcended gross sensual lust and gross ill-will, yet is he still possessed of them?
You should not say so… [and so on]…
Is the once-returner endowed with the fruit of stream-entry?
Yes. But is it not the case that the once-returner has transcended the fruit of stream-entry?
“Yes.
“If a once-returner has transcended the fruit of stream-entry, then surely it should not be said:
‘A once-returner is endowed with the fruit of stream-entry.’”
Is the once-returner one who has transcended the fruit of stream-entry and is possessed of it? Yes.
Has the once-returner transcended the path of stream-entry, and is he possessed of personality-belief … pe … and of the delusion that leads to states of deprivation? [No.]
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said that “an Arahant is endowed with the four fruits”?
“Yes.
“But surely the four fruits have been attained by the Arahant, and he has not fallen away from them?
“Yes.”
If an Arahant has attained the four fruits and has not fallen away from them, then indeed, sir, one should say:
"An Arahant is endowed with the four fruits.
But it should not be so said.
“Is a non-returner endowed with three fruits?”— Yes.
But has the non-returner not already attained those three fruits and not fallen away from them?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “If a non-returner has attained the three fruits and has not fallen away from them, then indeed, sir, it must be said:
‘A non-returner is endowed with the three fruits.’”
Is it not to be said that a once-returner is endowed with two fruits?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that a once-returner has attained two fruits and has not fallen away from them?
Yes, it is so.
If indeed a once-returner has attained two fruits and has not fallen away from them, then, indeed, it must be said:
“One who is a once-returner is endowed with two fruits.
Is an Arahant endowed with four fruits because he has attained the four fruits and has not fallen away from them? Yes.
If it is said that an Arahant has attained the four paths and has not fallen away from them, is it then to be said that the Arahant is endowed with the four paths?
Certainly not... [and so on].
If it is said that a Non-returner (Anāgāmin) has attained three fruits and has not fallen away from them, is it then to be said that the Non-returner is endowed with the three fruits?
[Opponent: Yes.
[Proponent: Since the non-returner has attained three paths and has not fallen away from them, must it not be said that the non-returner is endowed with three paths?
You should not say so …pe… [as before].
